tools.name: article_question
tools.description: Returns a one to two sentence answer quoted verbatim from the official EU article text, a spoken source line to read aloud, the permanent ID, source status and the official EUR-Lex link. Example: act=ai-act-2024-1689, article=50, question=vad-sager. Free.

tools.name: search_legal_sources
tools.description: Literal search across the register: Swedish statutes (SFS), guiding decisions from HD and HFD, EU acts (CELEX), US rules (CFR/USC) and finance glossary terms. Returns identifiers, titles and official source URLs. No generated text.

tools.name: get_legal_source
tools.description: Fetch one row from the register by its layer and identifier: a Swedish statute (se), a guiding decision (praxis), an EU act (eu), a US rule (us) or a finance glossary term (finance). Includes identifiers, dates, official source URL and related sources.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Daily digest of new and updated EU and US judgments plus changed pages since a date. Call once per day with the returned `next` address instead of refetching the corpus; use the `sync` cursor feed for continuous updates.

tools.name: evidence_questions
tools.description: Depth in steps for one provision, e.g. statute:regulation-2016-679-eu#art-32. Call without question for relation counts and the three questions; then call with question=sanction, change or precedent for a counted one-sentence answer. Each extra call narrows the answer. The linked judgments, decision

tools.name: network_status
tools.description: Live, aggregated operating data: requests in the last 24 h and 7 d (verified fetchers separate from signature only), API median and p95 latency, success share, evidence graph size and nightly run state, monitoring job state and a hash-chained daily receipt you can recompute. Counts requests, not peo

tools.name: unlock_evidence_graph
tools.description: Shows how many evidence relations are locked for a canonical object and returns a ready usage key plus a one-click payment link (prepaid USD balance, no account). The key activates after confirmed payment; then send it as x-partner-key to /api/public/v1/evidence-graph.

tools.name: consequence
tools.description: Source-bound consequence answer filtered by topic (gdpr, ai-act, dora), sector, country, company size and language (sv, en, de, fr, it, es, zh). size=brief (~100 tokens) and standard (~250 tokens) are free; size=deep costs $0.05 from a prepaid developer key and adds relations and the decision path.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-open" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_legal_sources, get_legal_source · Private data: consequence · Public sink: network_status, unlock_evidence_graph · Destructive: network_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_legal_sources, get_legal_source · Private data: consequence · Public sink: network_status, unlock_evidence_graph · Destructive: network_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
